## Instructions

Complete this tutorial while reading Chapter 8 of the [textbook](https://nustat.github.io/intro-stat-data-sci/08-populations.html). Each question allows 3 'free' attempts. After the third attempt a 10% deduction occurs per attempt.

You can click the "View Grade" button as many times as you would like to see your current grade and the number of attempts you are on. Before submitting make sure your grade is as expected.

### Goals

-   Understand the difference between population parameters and sample estimators.
-   Be able to identify the different types of sampling.
-   Describe the difference between random sampling and random assignment, and know the appropriate conclusions that can be drawn from each.
-   Be able to determine the extent to which a study's results can be generalized.


## Reading Quiz

```{r Q}
quiz(caption = NULL,
    # Q1 (NEW, 8.1)
    question("Q1) In the book's notation, what do $N$ and $n$ represent?",
           answer("$N$ is the population size and $n$ is the sample size.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("$N$ is the sample size and $n$ is the population size."),
           answer("$N$ is the number of variables and $n$ is the number of observations."),
           answer("$N$ and $n$ both represent the sample size."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q2 (8.1)
    question_wordbank("Q2) Match each statistic with its corresponding population parameter.",
           choices = c("\\(\\pi\\)", "\\(\\sigma\\)",
                       "\\(\\beta_1\\)", "\\(\\mu\\)",
                       "\\(\\rho\\)", "\\(\\beta_0\\)"),
           wordbank = c("proportion", "standard deviation",
                        "regression slope", "mean",
                        "correlation", "regression intercept"),
           answer(c("proportion", "standard deviation",
                    "regression slope", "mean",
                    "correlation", "regression intercept"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q3 (8.1)
    question_wordbank("Q3) Match each statistic with its corresponding sample estimator.",
           choices = c("\\(r\\)", "\\(b_0\\)",
                       "\\(\\widehat{\\pi}\\)", "\\(\\overline{x}\\)",
                       "\\(b_1\\)", "\\(s\\)"),
           wordbank = c("proportion", "standard deviation", "regression slope", "mean", "correlation", "regression intercept"),
           answer(c("correlation", "regression intercept",
                    "proportion", "mean", "regression slope",
                    "standard deviation"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q4 (8.1)
    question_wordbank("Q4) Match each of the following terms with whether it corresponds to a sample or a population.",
           choices = c("point estimate", "Roman letters", "census", "parameter", "hat notation", "Greek letters"),
           wordbank = c("sample", "population"),
           answer(c("sample", "sample", "population", "population", "sample", "population"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q5 (8.1)
    question("Q5) Which of the following are TRUE about $\\overline{x}$? Select all that apply.",
           answer("It is an estimator for $\\sigma$."),
           answer("It is a measure of 'spread'."),
           answer("It is a point estimate.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It is a measure of 'center'.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It is a population parameter."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q6 (NEW, 8.2)
    question("Q6) What is **undercoverage**?",
           answer("When the population frame differs from the population, so that parts of the population cannot be studied.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("When the sample size is too small to estimate the population parameter."),
           answer("When some people selected for the sample do not respond."),
           answer("When a census is used instead of a sample."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q7 (8.2)
    question_wordbank("Q7) Imagine you are conducting a survey among the Northwestern student body. You decide to sample 200 students. Match each of the following scenarios with the corresponding sampling procedure.",
           choices = c("50 students are randomly selected from each of the four classes (i.e. freshmen, sophomores, juniors, seniors)",
                       "200 students are randomly selected from a list of all NetIDs",
                       "20 courses are randomly selected, and then 10 students are randomly selected from each course",
                       "After a random starting point, every 10th student entering the student center is selected",
                       "The first 200 students who walk past the library are selected"),
           wordbank = c("stratified sampling",
                        "simple random sampling",
                        "cluster sampling",
                        "systematic sampling",
                        "convenience sampling"),
           answer(c("stratified sampling",
                    "simple random sampling",
                    "cluster sampling",
                    "systematic sampling",
                    "convenience sampling"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q8 (8.1 - 8.2)
    question("Q8) Which of the following statements are TRUE about random sampling? Select all that apply.",
           answer("Every unit in the population must have an equal probability of being selected."),
           answer("Every unit in the population must have a non-zero probability of being selected.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Individuals or units must be selected via a random process.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It enables us to generalize to the population we sampled from.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("It requires a population frame to be developed or obtained in advance.", correct = TRUE),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q9 (8.3)
    question_wordbank("Q9) Match each of the following steps in the sampling process with the order in which they should be conducted.",
           choices = c("1st step", "2nd step", "3rd step", "4th step", "5th step"),
           wordbank = c("Define your population of interest", "Develop a population frame", "Develop a sampling plan", "Obtain your sample", "Collect data on your sample"),
           answer(c("Define your population of interest", "Develop a population frame", "Develop a sampling plan", "Obtain your sample", "Collect data on your sample"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q10 (NEW, 8.3.2)
    question("Q10) In the movies example, why were movies released before 1930 excluded from the population of interest?",
           answer("The earliest movies were silent films, and dialogue did not become the norm until the 1930s.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("The IMDb database does not include movies released before 1930."),
           answer("Movies before 1930 were too short to be considered standard movies."),
           answer("Movies before 1930 had no IMDb user ratings."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q11 (NEW, 8.3.3)
    question_numeric("Q11) After applying all of the inclusion criteria in the movies example, what is the population size $N$?",
           answer(39123, correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q12 (NEW, 8.3.4)
    question("Q12) In the movies example, sampling 71 movies from each decade is an example of stratified sampling with:",
           answer("Unequal probabilities, because the decades contain different numbers of movies.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Equal probabilities, because the same number of movies is sampled from each decade."),
           answer("Equal probabilities, because every decade is included."),
           answer("No probabilities, because stratified sampling is not random."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q13 (NEW, 8.4)
    question("Q13) According to the reading, what should you do when you have a sample from an unclear population? Select all that apply.",
           answer("Assume the sample is a random sample from some population.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Define as clearly as you can what population the sample is from, using clear inclusion / exclusion criteria.", correct = TRUE),
           answer("Conclude that the results generalize to everyone."),
           answer("Discard the data, since no inferences can be made."),
           random_answer_order = TRUE,
           allow_retry = TRUE),
    # Q14 (8.5)
    question_wordbank("Q14) Match each of the following study types with the appropriate conclusions that can be drawn from them.",
           choices = c("Random assignment", "Neither random sampling nor random assignment", "Random sampling", "Random sampling + random assignment"),
           wordbank = c("Causal claim within your sample only",
                        "Associational claim within your sample only",
                        "Associational claim, generalized to the whole population",
                        "Causal claim, generalized to the whole population"),
           answer(c("Causal claim within your sample only",
                    "Associational claim within your sample only",
                    "Associational claim, generalized to the whole population",
                    "Causal claim, generalized to the whole population"), correct = TRUE),
           allow_retry = TRUE)
)
```
